beats.note: It began on the evening of 8 October 1871 in the O'Leary family barn on DeKoven Street. Smithsonian reports the Chicago Evening Journal implicated Catherine O'Leary before the fire died out.

beats.text: Nobody could say what started it.
beats.note: The 1871 inquiry reported, in Smithsonian and Mental Floss, that we are unable to determine the cause.

beats.text: A reporter made up the cow.
beats.note: Wikipedia, Ripley's and Mental Floss all report that Michael Ahern admitted he fabricated the story. Mental Floss says he and two colleagues invented it to add colour.

beats.context: About 300 people died and around 100,000 were left homeless, according to Smithsonian and Mental Floss. The blame landed on one woman.

beats.note: Smithsonian cites ethnic stereotypes and nativist fears. Ripley's names anti Irish and anti Catholic sentiment.

beats.name: Chicago City Council
beats.role: Formally exonerated Catherine O'Leary of responsibility for the fire. She had died on 3 July 1895.

beats.text: The city took 126 years to clear her name.

beats.line: The best story is not always the true one.
